name: Snap2Pass
description: Upload a selfie and it gets resized, background-fixed and checked against your country's exact document spec. It covers passport, visa and ID photos (founder-stated). Homepage: "500K+ photos processed", "166 countries supported", "99.8% acceptance rate", "ICAO 9303 compliant", "14-day money-back guarantee", free reshoots if rejected. It also offers same-day printing at Walgreens/CVS (~$0.39) or mailed prints ($7.47) (company-stated). There's a B2B tier for travel agencies and photo studios: a branded client photo link or upload at the counter, plus an API. Pricing: $20 for 4 clients, volume packs down to $2 a client, no subscription (company-stated). The app lists in-app purchases "starting at $4.99" (company-stated). ~20,000 estimated users (founder-stated). Founded Jan 2023, US, founder "oalpay". There's an AI headshot upsell too, but the core job is a government form requirement.

mentions.indieAngle: Do the EU/PL version. Polish passport and ID photos (zdjęcie do dowodu/paszportu) have a strict spec, and so do Schengen/US/UK/Chinese visa photos for Poles and Ukrainians in Poland. Sell to consumers at ~20 zł, and give fotograf studios and visa agencies a white-label link on credits.

whyItPrints: Consulates and passport offices reject bad photos, so people pay a few dollars to not get rejected. Demand comes from passport renewals, visa season and Google searches for "<country> visa photo size". The B2B side (agencies, studios) turns one-off buyers into repeat accounts.
